what: the widget's buffer landing whole on the device pixel grid
note: The first case file for `lib/src/widget/`. Until #110 the layer had no
mutation coverage at all, which is why the two regressions the
completeness pass caught — a squeezed box overflowing, and a leaf that
declines the hit test — had nothing standing over them.
Group A is the fix itself. A1 and A2 are the two roundings; A3 is the
coordinate space they are computed in.
A3 is the one that earned this file, and it earned it twice. It is the
half a rendered pixel cannot price: Skia with `isAntiAlias` off already
rounds a destination rectangle whose width is a whole number of device
pixels, so with A1 in place both A2 and A3 leave every screenshot in the
suite green. They die against `snappedAvatarRect` and
`debugGlobalDestination` instead — the placement asserted where it is
made rather than where it is drawn. Keeping the snap despite the backend
already doing it is invariant 4: leaning on Skia's rounding is the
Skia-versus-Impeller dependence the package exists to refuse.
Group B is what replacing a framework render object silently dropped.
Neither is a wrong number; both are a default that stopped being
supplied. B1 painted a 240-pixel avatar across a 20-logical box, over its
neighbours; B2 stopped taps reaching an enclosing `GestureDetector`, 0
against `RawImage`'s 1.
`test: null` means the whole suite, and it is not narrowed here even
though every assertion that kills these lives in `widget_test.dart`. The
layer is new to this harness and a narrowed run would report a golden
regression as a survivor — the same judgement #58 records.

cases.name: A1 — the extent is not rounded onto the grid
A2 — the origin is not snapped
A3 — the snap reads the enclosing layer instead of the screen
B1 — the drawn extent comes from the buffer, not the box
B2 — the leaf declines the hit test, as RenderBox does
